column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/pleme-ansible.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHY ANY OF THESE TABLES EXIST. On 2026-08-08 pleme-io/graphql-synthesizer ran
# cargo-auto-release. The run reported SUCCESS, bumped + tagged + pushed, and
# published nothing, because `ship` carried a `!private` guard that is entirely
# correct and that nobody had written down. A deliberate skip and a broken skip
# produced the same green tick. A table states which jobs MUST run for a given
# input, so the two stop looking alike.
# WHAT pleme-ansible IS. A pure TIER-2 DISPATCHER: ten sibling jobs, zero
# `needs:` edges, each gated on `inputs.target == '<its own id>'` and doing
# nothing but `uses:` the matching flat leaf. `inputs.target` is the ONLY
# context path any condition reads, so it is the only key declared per row. No
# condition calls always()/success()/failure()/cancelled(), and with no `needs:`
# anywhere, needs-propagation has nothing to propagate through — every verdict
# below is one `==` against one string.
# THE PROPERTY PINNED IS EXACTLY-ONE-SELECTS, which is why every row names all
# ten jobs — the nine that must skip as well as the one that must run. A row
# naming only its own arm cannot see a SECOND arm firing, and a dispatcher whose
# arms overlap silently runs two pipelines over one repo. The ten arm rows are
# deliberately mechanical: the claim is the whole ten-by-ten grid, not any one
# row.
# THE LAST TWO ROWS MATTER MOST, AND THEY RECORD A REAL HOLE. Nothing in this
# file is a catch-all: when `target` matches no arm, all ten jobs skip and the
# workflow reports SUCCESS having done nothing — the graphql-synthesizer shape
# exactly. Through the intended front door that is caught upstream, not here:
# pleme.yml's `validate` job greps THIS FILE for the literal
# `inputs.target == '<t>'` and exits 1 when it is absent, and rejects an empty
# target outright. But this composer's own header invites direct calls
# ("Calling it directly also works and simply spends one fewer chain level"),
# and on that path there is no `validate` at all. So `unknown-target-*` and
# `empty-target-*` are not hypotheticals — they are the direct-call posture,
# recorded rather than assumed. If a fail-loud catch-all job is ever added here,
# both rows go red and must be rewritten to expect it. That is the correct
# outcome, not a nuisance.
# CROSS-FAMILY IS THE REALISTIC UNKNOWN. pleme.yml takes `family` and `target`
# as two independent strings, so `family=ansible` paired with a rust target is a
# reachable operator slip rather than an invented value. The unknown row uses
# `cargo-auto-release` — a genuine target of another family — instead of a
# nonsense string, so the row models the mistake someone will actually make.
# PUBLISH / PUSH POSTURE. Two arms have outward-facing effects:
# `ansible-collection-release` builds the collection and publishes it to Ansible
# Galaxy, and `ansible-collection-auto-bump` commits, tags and pushes. The
# do-it input for each is its own arm row; the don't-do-it inputs are the other
# eleven rows, where both ids sit in expect-skip. Intended: selecting any other
# target must not publish to Galaxy and must not push a tag. Note that
# `ansible-collection-integration-live` reads outward-facing and is not — it is
# backed by a stdlib mock gateway, no external service is touched.
# WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. No near-miss / substring row (e.g.
# `ansible-collection-ci-extra`). Under today's `==` it asserts nothing the arm
# rows do not, and if an arm were ever loosened to startsWith()/contains() the
# linter REFUSES with an EVAL error naming the construct — on every row, not
# only a near-miss one. A row that cannot fail for its stated reason is a row
# the next person deletes.
# One per catalogued target of the `ansible` family. Each asserts its own arm
# runs AND that the other nine do not. Together they prove the arm set is a
# partition: total (every catalogued target reaches a leaf) and disjoint (no
# target reaches two).
target-ansible-test
target-auto-bump
target-auto-merge
target-ci
target-docs-lint
target-integration-live
target-matrix
target-published-install
target-release
target-upstream-watch
# A target belonging to a different family. Reachable because pleme.yml takes
# `family` and `target` as independent strings, and on a DIRECT call to this
# composer nothing validates the pairing at all. Ten skips, green run, no work
# done: the posture as it stands today, written down so that adding a fail-loud
# catch-all is a deliberate edit here rather than an unnoticed behaviour change.
unknown-target-cross-family
# The empty value is a DISTINCT state from any named target and from an unknown
# one: it is "the caller resolved `target` to nothing" — an unset `with:`, a
# `${{ inputs.target }}` that came through empty — rather than "the caller named
# something wrong". `target` is declared `required: true`, which GitHub enforces
# as present-but-possibly-empty, not as non-empty; pleme.yml adds the non-empty
# check itself, and a direct caller gets none. Same ten skips, same green run.
empty-target-selects-nothing
